We now choose which model variables enter the data.

::: {.lesson-links}

## Model

This extension concerns the observation equation for the particle filter. The economy and
calibration are those of [Extension 5](extension-05.qmd). So far, we have implicitly included
all five variables determined in the model, $\hat X_t$, $\hat\Pi_t$, $\hat I_t$, $\hat R_t^*$,
and $\widehat{mp}_t$. These data are observed with some measurement error. The measurement
equation is then given as

$$
\begin{bmatrix}\text{Output gap}\\\text{Inflation}\\\text{Interest rate}\\\text{Natural rate of interest}\\\text{Monetary policy shock}\end{bmatrix}
=\begin{bmatrix}\hat X_t\\\hat\Pi_t\\\hat I_t\\\hat R_t^*\\\widehat{mp}_t\end{bmatrix}+u_t,
$$

where the measurement error follows a Gaussian distribution $u_t\sim N(0,\Sigma_u)$. The
errors are independent across series, and the variance of the measurement error for each time
series is a fraction $m_E$ of its own variance. We set $m_E=0.1$.

In this extension, we are interested in only observing the output gap, inflation, and the
interest rate. The measurement equation is then given as

$$
\begin{bmatrix}\text{Output gap}\\\text{Inflation}\\\text{Interest rate}\end{bmatrix}
=\begin{bmatrix}\hat X_t\\\hat\Pi_t\\\hat I_t\end{bmatrix}+u_t.
$$

## Neural network solution

### Formulation

The policy network is unchanged. The filter still tracks all three states, but it uses only
the three observed variables to calculate the likelihood.

The loss is unchanged from [Extension 1](extension-01.qmd). It is the weighted mean of the squared residuals $F_1$ (Euler equation), $F_2$ (Phillips curve), and $F_3$ (Taylor rule), with expectations approximated by Monte Carlo shock draws.

### In the code

#### Select observations after evaluating policies

`forecast` advances the state and evaluates the policies, then `observe` selects the
variables in `OBSERVATION_NAMES`, here the output gap, inflation, and the nominal rate. Both the simulation and the particle filter call this
same method, so their observation definitions agree.

```{.python filename="examples/rank/rank_extension_06.py"}
def observe(self, obs_raw):
    # New in Extension 6: observe only the three policy variables.
    return {key: obs_raw[key] for key in self.OBSERVATION_NAMES}
```
::: {.code-source}
[View in `rank_extension_06.py` on GitHub]({{< meta repo-blob >}}/examples/rank/rank_extension_06.py)
:::

The notebook adds measurement noise after simulation and passes its covariance matrix
to `ParticleFilter`. The natural rate and monetary shock remain in the model even though we no longer
observe them.
